title: Introducing The Information's 50 Most Promising Startups of 2026
summary: The Information released its annual list of 50 promising early-stage startups, selected on revenue, business models and growth prospects, and for the first time added a dedicated security category. Three of the four most highly valued companies on the list are security startups worth more than $1 billion, and named picks include AI penetration-testing firm Tenzai, Nir Zuk's newly founded Cylake and Noitom Robotics. The publication notes past picks such as Cursor's maker, chosen at a $400 million valuation and later acquired by SpaceX for $60 billion.

title: Jensen Huang's Downfall
summary: WSJ Technology's weekly lead recaps Jensen Huang's rapid exit from Nvidia: within a week he acknowledged an affair with a woman U.S. authorities suspect of passing information to Chinese intelligence, a second affair with a longtime Nvidia executive triggered an emergency board meeting, and he resigned with CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO. The piece adds WSJ reporting that in his final months Huang clashed with Kress over Nvidia's use of its balance sheet to support cloud startups and backstop data-center projects, warning that an "avalanche" of purchase commitments threatened the company. Investors will hear from Kress when Nvidia reports earnings on Tuesday.

title: What It Takes to Deliver Your Wings Order During a Football Game, Fast and Hot
summary: The Wall Street Journal looks at how Wingstop relies on its digital ordering infrastructure, with a single order potentially drawing on about 40 different Amazon Web Services cloud services. Nearly 74% of the chain's third-quarter restaurant sales came through its app and online delivery and pickup channels, making fast, reliable technology central to its business during demand spikes such as football games.

title: How Jensen Huang Built the Backdoor Route That Keeps Beijing in the AI Race
summary: The Wall Street Journal examines how large data centers in Southeast Asia, built with Nvidia's cooperation under Jensen Huang, supplied crucial computing power to Chinese companies despite U.S. export controls. The report says these facilities also served as cover for alleged smuggling of restricted chips, adding a national-security dimension to the scandal surrounding Huang's departure.

title: Nvidia CEO Ouster Reverberates Globally
summary: Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO is rippling through the chip sector, AI startups and U.S.-China relations, as workarounds that let Chinese buyers access Nvidia chips may now close and the company's role as a funder of smaller AI firms shrinks. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged the board to pick an outside CEO, while the FT reported Huang has privately discussed a return and the board has approached Arm CEO Rene Haas. Interim CEO Colette Kress faces her first earnings call on Tuesday after the stock fell 13% last week.

title: The Investors Set to Win Big in Anthropic's IPO
summary: Anthropic's IPO this week is expected to value the Claude developer at $1.33 trillion or more, setting up large payouts for its more than 300 investors, from early angels in its 2021 Series A at a $461 million valuation to backers of its $965 billion Series H in May. The Information expects strong demand to push pricing above the $70–$78 preliminary range and a first-day open potentially well above $100 a share.

title: Nvidia's Days as an Open Checkbook for the AI Economy Are Numbered
summary: Nvidia's role as a major investor in AI startups and cloud partners is expected to shrink under interim CEO Colette Kress, after Huang had already told cloud partners they would need upfront customer payments to get GPUs. UBS estimates the pullback could remove $50 billion or more from the market, with pending deals involving Reflection AI and a planned investment in Thinking Machines Lab at a $40 billion valuation in doubt.

title: Trump Administration to Name Nvidia Among AI 'National Champions'
summary: The Trump administration plans to designate more than two dozen companies, including Nvidia, as AI 'national champions' to spread U.S. AI technology abroad. The designation brings faster export-license approvals, federal financing and government support overseas, and is proceeding despite investigations surrounding Nvidia's China sales.

title: California AG Accuses OpenAI of Misleading and Endangering the Public
summary: California's attorney general has sued OpenAI, alleging the company knowingly developed AI models without necessary safeguards and misled the public. The case is a significant state-level legal challenge to the ChatGPT maker.

title: Big Tech Needs to Spread Its Bets on Data Centers
summary: A Heard on the Street column argues that AI companies concentrating spending on a small number of mega data-center projects look exposed after the midterm elections. It makes the case for diversifying data-center bets to reduce political and execution risk.

title: Thomson Reuters CEO Says Content Is King When It Comes to AI
summary: Thomson Reuters CEO Steve Hasker says the company's proprietary content is its key advantage in AI and that it will keep investing heavily in AI-driven products. The interview reflects how information providers are positioning owned data as a moat against general-purpose AI models.

title: Verizon Trades Network Claims for Pop-Culture Buzz
summary: Under CMO Leslie Berland, who joined in 2024, Verizon has moved away from network-reliability messaging toward pop-culture-driven ads featuring TV heartthrobs, and is building an in-house team to produce ads faster. One spot was pulled after alienating viewers 55 and older, and some observers doubt buzzy ads will get customers to switch carriers.

title: Gucci Is Cutting Prices; Louis Vuitton Is Reluctant to Follow the Trend
summary: Luxury executives are openly debating price cuts to escape a three-year slump as mid-tier luxury growth has evaporated, with LVMH's CFO acknowledging internal discussions while still opposing cuts at Louis Vuitton. Gucci has already reduced prices on some items, including a bag that fell 30% from €3,500 to €2,450 in France since July.

title: Microsoft Data Shows Claude Is Stalling Against Copilot in Office
summary: Internal Microsoft data reviewed by The Information indicates that Anthropic's push to get Claude used inside Office apps has stalled relative to Microsoft's own Copilot. The report lands days before Anthropic's IPO and bears on its enterprise productivity ambitions.

title: OpenAI Explored $5 Billion–Plus Acquisition of Startup That Decodes How AI 'Thinks'
summary: OpenAI previously explored acquiring an AI interpretability startup, which works on decoding how AI models reason internally, for at least $5 billion, according to The Information. The talks highlight the rising strategic value placed on interpretability research among frontier labs.

title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Digital Wallet
summary: OpenAI announced a ChatGPT digital wallet that lets its Dot assistant make online purchases without directly accessing shoppers' card details. The move extends OpenAI's push into agentic commerce.

title: Alibaba Unveils New Flagship AI Model Qwen4-Max
summary: Alibaba added Qwen4-Max as the new flagship of its Qwen family, the world's most downloaded open-weight model series. Alibaba says it beats Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 and Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro on coding benchmarks, though unlike most Qwen models it is not open weight.

title: Nokia, Telia Target EU AI Compute Needs
summary: Nokia and Telia lead a Nordic consortium formed to build an AI gigafactory, aiming to win business under a European initiative to create a supercomputing leader. The bid positions Nordic telecom and infrastructure players in the EU's push for sovereign AI compute.

title: Millicom Inks $1.7B Deal for Entel Peru
summary: Millicom signed an agreement to buy Entel Peru for $1.7 billion including lease liabilities. The acquisition would expand the group's footprint to 13 Latin American markets.

title: FCC Tees Up April 2027 for Upper C-Band Auction
summary: The U.S. FCC will open bidding in its upper C-Band spectrum auction on April 27, 2027. Chair Brendan Carr pitched the auction as creating a 5G 'super band' unmatched by other industrialized countries.

title: JPMorgan Chase Software Bug Disrupts Payments Across U.S. Banks
summary: A software bug in JPMorgan Chase's on-premises hardware disrupted transactions for hours on Monday, with payment delays spilling over to Bank of America, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo and Truist whenever Chase was a counterparty. Chase said there was no evidence of a cyberattack and processing returned to normal by early evening; it was the third major U.S. system failure in five days, after a Microsoft 365 outage and a nationwide FAA ground stop.

title: Nvidia Beats Estimates in First Earnings Report After Jensen Huang's Ouster
summary: Nvidia topped Wall Street expectations in its first quarterly report since founding CEO Jensen Huang was pushed out. Interim CEO Colette Kress was expected to face extensive investor questions about leadership, export-control exposure and the company's direction.

title: Anthropic Plans to Raise IPO Price After Strong Demand
summary: Anthropic intends to lift the price range of its initial public offering after strong investor demand during its roadshow. The pitch held up despite market turbulence and the shock resignation of Nvidia's Jensen Huang, ahead of the company's planned public debut this week.

title: Alice Huang's Husband Built a Data-Center Empire Backed by the Chinese State
summary: The WSJ reports that Kang Wei, husband of Alice Huang, built a data-center business with backing from the Chinese state while his wife was involved with Nvidia's then-CEO Jensen Huang. The report adds to the scrutiny of Nvidia's China ties that preceded Huang's resignation.

title: OpenAI Partners With NATO On Cyber Defenses
summary: OpenAI is making its advanced cybersecurity models available to NATO, whose technology and cyber hub of more than 3,000 civilian and military experts is using them to probe suspicious activity, find vulnerabilities and deploy fixes. The deal extends OpenAI's push into government and security work.

title: Genesis AI, a Robotics Startup, Raises $500 Million
summary: Robotics startup Genesis AI has raised $500 million to pursue what CEO Zhou Xian describes as the world's best general-purpose robot. The round is one of the larger recent bets on AI-driven robotics.

title: Nvidia Forms National-Security Committee After Huang's Exit
summary: Nvidia is creating a board committee to oversee national-security policy, export-control compliance and global trade risks following Jensen Huang's departure. The move responds to allegations about chip smuggling into China and mounting government scrutiny of the company.

title: Lush's CEO Says He Learned His Leadership Values in Grade School
summary: Lush co-founder and CEO Mark Constantine discussed a new parental-leave policy for North American full-time staff and the fallout from the retailer's Gaza awareness campaign, which ended its relationship with landlord Westfield Australia and will require relocating 10 mall stores as leases expire. The private company reported 9.2% brand sales growth for fiscal 2025 while facing cocoa-cost and tariff pressures.

title: Nvidia Directors Should Explain
summary: Martin Peers argues Nvidia's board must explain why it pushed Jensen Huang to resign, after reversing its earlier stated confidence in him, or face a growing reinstatement campaign backed by investors and even President Trump. Shareholders owning 15% for a year could call a special meeting, though that bar is hard to reach; Nvidia shares fell another 4% Monday to $156.14, down 35% since early October.
also_covered_by: The Globe and Mail Business Brief

title: Commerce Department Restricts Chinese AI Firms' Remote Access to U.S. Chips
summary: The Bureau of Industry and Security issued a long-awaited rule barring Chinese AI companies from using overseas data centres, mainly in Southeast Asia, to access export-controlled chips. Shares of Chinese AI firms MiniMax and Z.ai fell on fears of tighter chip access after Jensen Huang's resignation.

title: Blackstone Data-Center REIT Buys Stakes in AWS Joint Ventures
summary: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust is acquiring 75% stakes in two joint ventures with Amazon Web Services, valuing the deal at about $5 billion. It launches the REIT's strategy of buying data centres with long-term leases to major cloud providers.

title: How Google's New AI Chip Software Helps It Battle Nvidia
summary: Google's open-source TorchTPU lets developers run existing PyTorch workloads on its TPUs with minimal code changes, aiming to erode the lock-in of Nvidia's CUDA software. Paired with Nvidia's leadership turmoil, cloud firms report growing interest in AMD and Google chips; Morgan Stanley forecasts TPU hardware sales could top $81 billion next year, though one cloud-spending tracker counts only 16 of about 5,000 clients using TPUs at scale.

title: How JPMorgan, Citi Missed Megaspeed Risks in a $2.8 Billion Data Center Loan
summary: JPMorgan and Citigroup lent in 2025 to a Southeast Asian data-center operator that did business with Megaspeed, a company at the centre of the Nvidia and Jensen Huang scandal. The case highlights banks' indirect exposure to problematic firms through borrowers and raises questions about due diligence on complex ownership structures in the region.

title: OpenAI's Astra Is a Boon to Robotics, Says Nvidia Robotics Chief Deepu Talla
summary: Nvidia robotics head Deepu Talla called OpenAI's Astra model, released in September, a breakthrough for general-purpose robots because of its grasp of the physical world. He said it has made some kinds of robot-training data 100 times faster to create and could help automate deploying robots in factories.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: The $31-Billion Quebecor Bid That Would Reshape Telecom
summary: Quebecor has made an unsolicited, non-binding proposal to acquire Telus for about $31 billion, offering $6.35 in cash plus 0.17 Quebecor shares per Telus share, roughly a 60% premium. A deal would cut Canada's big telecom carriers from four to three and test competition law, needing approval from several agencies and Industry Minister Mélanie Joly; Telus has formed a special committee to review it.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: The Risky Business of Data Centres in Alberta
summary: Alberta's push to attract AI data centres, including Meta's $13-billion project, has drawn more than 145 announced facilities, over 75% of Canada's total, as the province targets $100 billion of investment in five years. Globe reporting finds growing rural dissent over rushed consultations and land deals, which could prove politically costly for Premier Danielle Smith after data centres hurt Republicans in U.S. midterms.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: Canaccord CEO Launches $1.6-Billion Take-Private Bid
summary: Canaccord Genuity CEO Dan Daviau has launched a $1.6-billion bid at $15.27 a share to take the investment dealer private. It is the second time the firm's leadership team has attempted a management buyout.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: TC Energy Expects 25% Rise in NGTL Pipeline Demand
summary: TC Energy says it will soon finalize its NOVA Gas Transmission annual plan, which projects total demand on the system to rise 25% over the next five years. The outlook reflects rising Western Canadian gas needs, including from proposed data centres.

title: Vulcan Rocket Failure Destroys 40 Amazon Leo Satellites
summary: United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket failed about 10 minutes into flight, destroying all 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites aboard in the first total mission failure in ULA's 20-year history. Amazon has about 400 Leo satellites in orbit against a need for more than 3,200, and the setback widens Starlink's lead.

title: Hyperscale Data Centers Rival Denmark's Emissions
summary: Harvard research on 403 U.S. hyperscale data centres estimates they used 82 TWh of electricity from May 2024 to April 2025, about 1.8% of U.S. demand, and emitted roughly 25.7 million metric tons of CO2, comparable to Denmark. About 54% of their power came from fossil fuels, and Virginia, Oregon, Ohio and Iowa accounted for over half of consumption.

title: Nvidia Highlights 3 Early AI-RAN Use Cases
summary: Nvidia's VP for AI and telecoms, Soma Velayutham, outlined three credible AI-RAN use cases and admitted the sudden rise of integrated sensing and communications had surprised the company. Separately, T-Mobile US said it will soon run AI-RAN and sensing trials on its road to 6G.

title: Orange Commits Additional €250M to VC Fund
summary: Orange allocated €250 million in fresh capital to its venture fund to back companies in sectors core to its strategic plan. The move expands the operator's investment in startups aligned with its growth priorities.

title: Nvidia's Interim CEO Has a Tough Challenge: Keep the Growth, Leave the Baggage
summary: In her first earnings call as interim CEO, Colette Kress reported record quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion, with data-center sales up 110%, and raised Nvidia's fiscal 2028 revenue-growth forecast from 70% to 75%. Board chair Harvey Jones ruled out reinstating Jensen Huang despite a petition nearing 200,000 signatures, while questions over past deals and succession persist. Separately, a filing showed Nvidia sold more than half of its Nokia stake in the July–September quarter.
also_covered_by: The Globe and Mail Business Brief

title: Anthropic Prices IPO at $83 a Share on Strong Demand
summary: Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 a share and sold more shares than originally planned after heavy investor demand. The listing, reported as multiple times oversubscribed and on track to be the largest stock debut ever, is being watched as a major test of investor appetite for the AI boom.
also_covered_by: The Globe and Mail Business Brief

title: What's Behind the String of Tech Outages Disrupting Business and Travel
summary: A week of outages hitting Microsoft, the FAA, JPMorgan, United Airlines, Apple and the NSA's classified network has been traced to botched patches and upgrades rather than coordinated hacking, officials say. AI tools are uncovering software flaws at record pace — Microsoft's latest monthly update fixed about 1,400 vulnerabilities versus roughly 170 a year earlier — forcing rapid, automated patching that can break systems.

title: Palo Alto Networks to Buy AI-Startup Applied Compute for $4.5 Billion
summary: Palo Alto Networks agreed to acquire Applied Compute for $4.5 billion. The startup, founded last year by former OpenAI researchers, specializes in customizing open-weight AI models for enterprises.

title: SEC Is Probing Nvidia Amid Departure of CEO Jensen Huang
summary: The Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia following Jensen Huang's resignation, according to people familiar with the matter. The probe's full scope is unclear but includes whether the company's disclosures misled investors; Nvidia had earlier denied Huang had an unusual relationship with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive U.S. officials believe works for Chinese intelligence.

title: U.S. Officials Urge Immediate Patching of 'Java4Shell' Flaw
summary: U.S. officials urged companies and agencies to immediately patch a critical bug in Oracle's Java development tools that could crash systems and allow remote takeover; Oracle's latest critical update contains 655 security patches. The flaw was discovered with AI by Calif Research, which estimates about 90% of Fortune 500 companies run relevant Java tools.

title: Waymo Restricts Freeway Operations After California Ban
summary: Waymo temporarily restricted its robotaxis from U.S. freeways after California regulators banned its self-driving cars from freeways in the state. Officials cited several incidents involving Waymo vehicles.

title: Bret Taylor's Sierra in Talks to Raise at $30 Billion Valuation
summary: Sierra, the AI customer-service agent startup co-founded by Bret Taylor, is in talks to raise funding at a $30 billion valuation. The round would roughly double the company's previous valuation.

title: Microsoft Nears $500 Million Deal to Sell AI to ByteDance, Irking OpenAI
summary: ByteDance is in talks to spend roughly an additional $500 million on Microsoft's Azure cloud, largely to access OpenAI models. The arrangement has irritated OpenAI, highlighting tension over how Microsoft resells its partner's technology.

title: Nvidia Introduced Alibaba to Alice Huang for Workaround on U.S. Export Controls
summary: Nvidia's sales team twice introduced Alibaba to Alice Huang, the alleged Chinese spy tied to smuggling Nvidia chips into China, in 2022 before U.S. export controls took effect, according to people with direct knowledge. The introductions helped her company win Alibaba as a customer, which in turn helped it secure bank loans to buy Nvidia chips.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: OMERS Teams Up in Bid for Underwater Toronto Transmission Line
summary: OMERS and Blackstone-owned Transmission Developers Infrastructure plan a joint bid to build the 65-kilometre Toronto Third Line, a high-voltage cable along the bottom of Lake Ontario linking the Darlington nuclear station to downtown Toronto. The roughly $1.5-billion project, Ontario's first underwater transmission line, is meant to add capacity and redundancy and enter service by 2037.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: Experts Call for National Security Review of Moneris Deal
summary: Security and digital experts say Francisco Partners' $2-billion purchase of Moneris, which handles about one in three Canadian card transactions, should face a full national security review under the Investment Canada Act. They cite data-sovereignty concerns and the private equity firm's past ownership of surveillance-technology companies; the Competition Bureau is already reviewing the deal.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: PBO Flags Debt Costs as Fastest-Growing Federal Expense
summary: Parliamentary Budget Officer Annette Ryan said public debt charges are the fastest-growing federal expense in her assessment of the 2026 budget. The PBO said the government promised to spend less to invest more but instead spends more, invests more and borrows more.

title: Ukraine's Vulnerability Highlights Need for U.S. Satellite Alternatives, Carney Says
summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney said SpaceX's throttling of Starshield service in Ukraine shows why Canada is seeking access to European Union satellite systems for Arctic security. Ottawa and Brussels agreed last month to negotiate Canadian participation in the Galileo navigation program and explore co-operation on the IRIS2 secure network.

title: Loblaw to Let Canadians Buy Groceries Through Meta's Muse AI Agent
summary: Loblaw became the first Canadian retailer to partner directly with Meta's Muse, letting customers browse and complete grocery purchases through the AI agent without visiting its site or app. The move contrasts with Canada's major banks, most of which have blocked or restricted third-party AI agents, and with Amazon, which has blocked Muse.

title: Scammers Are Infiltrating Bay Street With Social Engineering
summary: A wave of breaches at Canadian law firms including McCarthy Tétrault, Bennett Jones, Borden Ladner Gervais and Davies reflects cyber criminals using fake documents and AI-enabled vishing to impersonate IT staff. Law firms are attractive targets because they control trust accounts, and IBM data shows AI-driven attacks rose 56% over the past year.

title: Mississauga Faces Legal Challenge Over Data-Centre Moratorium
summary: Prologis and Toronto asset manager Montcrest have appealed Mississauga's one-year pause on data centres drawing more than 10 megawatts, arguing it creates land-use uncertainty and delays investment. The bylaw halted a proposed 40-megawatt Prologis facility; Mississauga is one of at least six Ontario municipalities to pause data-centre development.

title: Boards Governing AI and Workforce as One
summary: A Deloitte survey of 806 board members and C-suite executives in 53 countries found only 16% of organizations have an established strategy for AI's impact on their workforce. Nearly half say boards do not consistently factor human capital into AI discussions, and just 12% have full oversight of how tech budgets split between infrastructure and people.

title: Why AI Costs Are Outrunning Budgets
summary: Capgemini's survey of 500 executives at $1B-plus companies found nearly 60% overspent their AI budgets in the past year, by 24% on average, as agentic workloads drive up token usage. Six in ten lack an enterprise-wide view of AI costs, while open-weight models handle up to 72% of gateway tokens but only 14–27% of spend.

title: Inside BCG's Own AI Transformation
summary: BCG detailed its own AI transformation as 'client zero,' investing more than $3 billion over three years; over 90% of its 33,000-plus staff now use AI and about 60% do so habitually. The firm structures the effort around deploying tools, reshaping workflows and inventing new client offerings, with an internal agent marketplace cutting some cycle times two- to threefold.

title: T-Mobile US Adds 600MHz Spectrum
summary: T-Mobile US filed with the FCC to buy 58 licences in the 600MHz band from Bluewater Wireless. The low-band spectrum could strengthen its 5G coverage across 27 states.

title: Huawei Poised to Top Pre-Sanction Sales Peak
summary: Huawei is on track in 2026 to significantly surpass its 2020 revenue peak of CNY891.4 billion despite expanding western trade sanctions. Its diversification beyond telecom equipment and smartphones is credited for the rebound.

title: Anthropic Shares Close Up After Historic IPO
summary: Anthropic began trading on Nasdaq after an IPO that raised $81 billion at $83 a share, above its marketed $70–$78 range, valuing the Claude developer at about $1.5 trillion. The stock opened roughly 34% above the offer price, briefly implying a value near $2 trillion, and closed higher on its first day. The debut is expected to produce gains for early backers including Canadian pension funds and to spawn new AI investment products for Canadian investors.
also_covered_by: The Globe and Mail Business Brief

title: Thousands of Anthropic Employees and Investors Are Set to Reap Fortunes
summary: Most of Anthropic's more than 5,000 employees are expected to become millionaires as a result of the company's IPO. The Information separately examined whether the payday could trigger departures once lockups end and staff can sell shares.

title: Is Anthropic Worth $1.1 Trillion, or $1.5 Trillion? How to Make Sense of the Valuations
summary: Heard on the Street explains why different valuation figures are circulating for Anthropic. Its complex share structure and funding arrangements mean the headline number varies widely depending on which shares and commitments are counted.

title: Anthropic vs. OpenAI: The Financial Metrics Behind the AI Battle
summary: A WSJ comparison of the two leading AI labs finds that Anthropic heads into its public debut with higher revenue than OpenAI and smaller losses. The analysis lays out the financial metrics investors are using to weigh the rivals.

title: Anthropic Pushes the Reset Button for AI
summary: The Morning Download argues that Anthropic's IPO filings give investors hard data on AI demand, including $900.9 billion in aggregate compute commitments, $70.7 billion of which come due within 12 months. Analysts say the debate now shifts to margins versus growth, while other demand signals, such as Alibaba's and Lenovo's results, point to continued AI spending.

title: Nvidia Is the Central Bank to AI's Circular Economy. See Where the Money Goes.
summary: Nvidia has made at least 293 deals since 2023 and built an investment portfolio worth more than $100 billion, much of it in companies that buy its chips, including a $10 billion commitment to Anthropic's IPO. The eight public companies in its portfolio have lost a combined $820 billion in market value since Oct. 6, and interim CEO Colette Kress has said the company will be more disciplined about future deals.

title: Wall Street Pledged to Mobilize $500 Billion for Nvidia—But Hasn't Put Up a Dime
summary: In August, Jensen Huang got six Wall Street firms, including Apollo, Blackstone and Goldman Sachs, to pledge $500 billion to help Nvidia customers finance chip purchases. According to the WSJ, none of that money has been deployed.

title: Uber Co-Founder Kalanick Teases Protest at Nvidia as Calls for Huang's Return Continue
summary: Nvidia's board has said Jensen Huang will not return as CEO, but prominent tech figures are still lobbying for it. Travis Kalanick said he would lead a walkout at Nvidia's offices, Elon Musk compared the ouster to benching Michael Jordan, and Sam Altman said it was hard to imagine the AI industry without Huang.

title: See How Data Centers Became the Growth Engine of America's Power Grid
summary: Electricity use by U.S. commercial customers, a category that includes data centers, is on track to exceed residential demand this year for the first time. The WSJ graphic shows how AI-driven data-center construction has become the main source of growth in U.S. power demand.

title: Walmart Beats Forecasts as E-Commerce Sales Jump 17%
summary: Walmart's quarterly revenue rose 5.2% to $188.8 billion, ahead of forecasts. Global e-commerce sales grew 17%, or 23% in the U.S., and U.S. advertising revenue rose 37%. The CFO described the company's stores and delivery networks as increasingly digital assets.

title: Alibaba Earnings Rebound Sharply as AI Profitability Improves
summary: Alibaba's net profit roughly tripled to about $9.7 billion in the September quarter, well above forecasts, as its AI cloud and e-commerce businesses both became more profitable. The company has committed more than $53 billion over three years to AI hardware and software. Its shares are still down about 10% this week after new U.S. chip-export restrictions.

title: Lenovo Maintains Revenue Momentum on AI-Fueled Hardware Demand
summary: Lenovo's September-quarter revenue rose 48% to $30.2 billion, beating forecasts, as AI server demand more than doubled sales in its data-center business. The world's largest PC maker is on pace for $100 billion in annual revenue even as supply constraints weigh on global PC shipments.

title: Where Commerce Actually Begins
summary: At the WSJ CMO Council Summit, Visa CMO Frank Cooper III said AI agents will increasingly handle routine purchases such as detergent, while identity-driven shopping will stay human. He said marketers now have to sell to agents ('B to AI'), which makes product catalogs and brand websites more important, and that Visa must keep its brand memorable as payments become frictionless.

title: If You Thought AI Was Bad, Wait Until You Hear About the Drones
summary: At the Aspen Cyber Summit, current and former U.S. officials warned that cyber-physical threats are rising, including sabotage of undersea cables and drone strikes on data centers. An FCC national-security official said cable security is a recurring concern for the agency, which licenses cable landings in U.S. waters.

title: Equinor Investigates Cyberattack
summary: Norwegian energy company Equinor, one of Europe's largest natural gas suppliers, is working to contain a cyberattack that disrupted internal IT systems, including email. The company said oil and gas production was unaffected and it had no indication of data theft, but it could not say when systems would be fully restored.

title: Tech Stocks Boosted by Cybersecurity Rally
summary: Cybersecurity stocks rallied after a string of major technology outages: Okta jumped 12%, and Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike were among the market's best performers. The gains helped the Nasdaq end a four-session losing streak, as investors bet on higher corporate security spending.

title: Anthropic's IPO Eve
summary: Martin Peers argues that Anthropic's public-market path may not resemble Google's after its IPO. Anthropic generated $5.6 billion in free cash flow in the first nine months of the year, but that will shrink as it leases chips and runs its own data centers. It carries $452 billion in purchase and lease commitments due by 2030, against $33 billion of nine-month revenue and an $81 billion annualized run rate, so any slowdown in growth would be costly.

title: Anthropic Is Pushing New Products, and Big Discounts, to Justify Its Huge Valuation
summary: Anthropic is offering new products and steep discounts to expand beyond its core coding business and support its valuation. The push covers tools such as Claude Cowork and Managed Agents that automate legal, finance, HR and sales work.

title: ServiceNow Builds an AI Weapon to Target Salesforce Customers
summary: ServiceNow has released an AI tool that it says cuts the time to migrate customers onto its CRM software from six months to six weeks by automating data extraction. Oracle, SAP, Workday and Salesforce are building similar switching tools to win customers from each other. EY says adoption is still limited because customers usually wait for contracts to expire, and Anthropic's expanding enterprise tools add a further threat to established SaaS vendors.

title: Meta Bets on $300 Muse Charm to Boost AI Hardware Business
summary: Meta plans to price its upcoming pocket-sized Muse Charm AI device at $300 and offer user subsidies. The company hopes the gadget will lift its hardware business and draw users to its new personal assistant.

title: China's Moonshot AI Scraps $150 Million Deal to Access Nvidia Chips in Indonesia
summary: Moonshot AI, the Beijing developer of the Kimi models, has canceled a $150 million contract to rent Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 chips in an Indonesian data center. The move follows a new U.S. Commerce Department rule that closes the loophole allowing Chinese firms to access restricted chips remotely through overseas facilities.

title: U.S. Commerce Department Rushed to Clear Nvidia H200 Exports to China
summary: Jeffrey Kessler, who oversees the Bureau of Industry and Security, pressured staff to speed approvals of Nvidia H200 sales to China, in some cases over objections from other agencies, according to people familiar with the matter. President Trump approved H200 sales to China in December 2025 after lobbying by Jensen Huang, with the U.S. government taking a 25% cut.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: Stolen Faces, Fake News and Cross-Border Division
summary: A McGill-based research centre identified a network of at least 293 Instagram and TikTok accounts that used AI to hijack the faces of 226 real creators and spread false stories about the Canada-U.S. trade war. One fabricated claim, that Carney cancelled $8 billion in U.S. defence contracts, appeared in 161 videos with more than five million views. Researchers could not identify who runs the network, though activity patterns point to East or Southeast Asia.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: BCE Held Talks With Telus as It Weighs Response to Quebecor Bid
summary: BCE has held early talks with Telus and hired advisers after Quebecor went public with a $31 billion takeover proposal for the Vancouver telecom company. BCE would weigh what concessions Ottawa might demand before making any formal offer, while the Quebecor bid has already raised regulatory concerns.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: Carney Contrasts 'Very Professional' Chinese Trade Talks With Elusive U.S. Deal
summary: Speaking remotely from Shenzhen, Prime Minister Mark Carney said China had negotiated 'in a very linear fashion' toward a newly announced trade deal, while a U.S. agreement 'should have been done six months ago.' He suggested Canada will keep hedging its reliance on the U.S. even under a future administration.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: Client Files at KPMG Canada Compromised in Data Breach
summary: KPMG Canada is contacting clients whose tax documents were exposed in a recent data breach. It is the latest in a string of attacks on professional-services firms, after Bay Street law firms McCarthy Tétrault, Davies, Bennett Jones and BLG also reported breaches in recent weeks.

title: Huang's Nvidia Exit Puts Financing of Canada's AI Boom Under Scrutiny
summary: Nvidia has bankrolled much of the AI infrastructure buildout and now plans to be more selective with its investments after Jensen Huang's departure. The Logic reports that the shift could squeeze neocloud and compute companies expanding in Canada.

title: Businesses Want the Agency That Replaces BDC and EDC to Take Bigger Swings
summary: Business leaders say the new entity formed by merging the Business Development Bank of Canada and Export Development Canada needs deeper pockets and more appetite for risk than either predecessor. They argue that is necessary to help Canadian firms scale.

title: Qualcomm VP Argues Case for 6G Hardware Overhaul
summary: Qualcomm engineering VP Hemanth Sampath said 6G offers operators opportunities in core connectivity and compute, but may require a hardware overhaul. He urged telcos to upgrade to 5G-Advanced to start the transition. At the same event, Vodafone's R&D head warned that 6G must show a strong business case given how well standalone 5G performs.

title: Microsoft Teams With Intel Foundry
summary: Microsoft is using Intel Foundry for advanced packaging of its in-house Azure chips. The deal also secures a multi-year supply of Intel Xeon server processors.

title: Reliance Plans Satellite Network to Take On Starlink
summary: Reliance Industries is reportedly exploring manufacturing partnerships for a planned low-Earth-orbit broadband constellation of about 1,600 satellites, which would position it to compete with Starlink in India.

title: Anthropic's Mega IPO Lives Up to Wall Street Hype but Fails to Revive AI Trade
summary: Anthropic's shares closed 17% above their IPO price in Thursday's debut, valuing the company at roughly $1.3 trillion, or close to $1.8 trillion on a fully diluted basis. The strong debut did not lift the broader AI trade: North American markets closed sharply lower, Japan's Nikkei fell more than 5% overnight, and Anthropic's own shares were down as much as 10% in Friday premarket trading.
also_covered_by: The Globe and Mail Business Brief

title: Anthropic Shares Are a Rational Bet on the Next Phase of AI
summary: Heard on the Street columnist Asa Fitch argues that Anthropic's listing marks the start of a third phase of the AI boom, in which profits shift from infrastructure suppliers to the companies applying the technology. The column contends that, despite worries about infrastructure spending, demand for AI is real enough to justify the bet on Anthropic's shares.

title: White House Replaces Cybersecurity Official After Tech Outages
summary: National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is leaving his post and will be succeeded by Kirsten Davies, the Defense Department's chief information officer. The change follows a string of major outages, including one that left more than 450 million Microsoft 365 users unable to use email, and a wave of cyber threats tied to AI-armed hackers. A person familiar with the matter said President Trump backed the move over doubts about Cairncross's credentials.

title: Tech Outages Are Inevitable. Business Chaos Doesn't Have to Be.
summary: After a week of disruptions across email, air travel, banking and government communications, CIOs and CISOs told the WSJ that companies should plan for resilience rather than assume outages can be prevented. Their advice includes joint IT and security decision-making, realistic tabletop exercises, clear lines of authority during incidents, rollback options and staged rollouts for software updates. They also said AI-driven automation is needed for defence, but under human oversight.

title: Financial, Healthcare Companies Fell For Near-Perfect Deepfakes
summary: AI is producing increasingly convincing voice and video impersonations of executives, and financial and healthcare firms have been fooled by them. U.S. officials recently warned of a scheme called FaceStealer that has taken more than $400 million in crypto, and the Justice Department arrested three people accused of stealing over $100 million by directing employees to wire funds offshore.

title: Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Customer Data Leaked by Hackers
summary: A ransomware group called n0n leaked data on thousands of Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Chase customers after breaching third-party entities. The companies said services were not disrupted. The leak added to a week of high-profile tech and security incidents.

title: States Move to Block Disney's Bid for Character.AI Assets
summary: About 40 U.S. states objected to bankrupt chatbot maker Character Technologies' proposed $20 million sale of assets to Disney. They argue the deal could transfer users' private conversations, including those of minors, and threatens consumer privacy.

title: Databricks In Early Talks To Raise Funds At $225 Billion Valuation
summary: Data and AI software company Databricks is in early talks to raise new funding at a $225 billion valuation. That would be an increase of nearly 20% from the valuation it reached in August.

title: Anthropic Mathematician Says AI Has Solved the Most Famous Problem in Math
summary: An Anthropic mathematician says the company's Claude model helped find a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, which has been unsolved for 167 years. The claim came a day after Anthropic's IPO and has not yet been independently verified.

title: American State Capitalism Helped Produce the Nvidia Scandal
summary: This WSJ analysis argues that under President Trump, government and corporate interests have become more closely intertwined, and that this helped set the stage for the Nvidia scandal. It suggests the backlash against Nvidia could slow or halt the trend.

title: California Attorney General Issues Investigative Subpoena to Nvidia
summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta issued an investigative subpoena to Nvidia, opening a probe into the chip maker's conduct. The investigation follows revelations about former CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

title: China’s AI Firms Are Addicted to Nvidia Chips. Now They Are Facing Withdrawal.
summary: New U.S. measures cutting Chinese companies off from high-end computing power, including Nvidia chips accessed through overseas data centres, are a significant setback for Beijing's AI ambitions. Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu said the rule will affect the company's products and services next year.

title: AMD Shares Drop 9% After Hunterbrook Report on China Ties
summary: Advanced Micro Devices shares fell 9% on Thursday after short-selling research firm Hunterbrook Capital published a report on AMD's business relationships in China. The report cited ties to companies blacklisted by the U.S. government.

title: Bending Spoons to Buy Mailchimp From Intuit for $3.68 Billion
summary: Italian software group Bending Spoons agreed to buy email-marketing service Mailchimp from Intuit for $3.68 billion, mostly in cash. Bending Spoons also said it raised $1.3 billion in equity through a private placement with existing shareholders.

title: Google Taps Blue Origin to Launch Project Suncatcher Satellites
summary: Google will use Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin to launch satellites for Project Suncatcher, its experiment in running AI chips on solar power in orbit, on a dedicated New Glenn mission planned for the first quarter of 2029. Each satellite is meant to carry roughly a data-centre rack's worth of Google TPUs. The mission will test whether heat, radiation and maintenance problems can be managed in space.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: Finding the AI Choke Points
summary: The Globe's Future of Work reporter found that Canadian AI adoption is held back mainly by distrust of tool accuracy and by inadequate worker training, especially at smaller firms. Large banks have moved faster: TD's custom virtual assistant is used by 19,000 tellers, and BMO says about 58,000 employees now use Microsoft Copilot. The Carney government is counting on workplace AI adoption to lift Canada's long-lagging productivity.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: Ottawa Open to Telecom Takeovers That Would Leave Three Major Players
summary: Sources say the federal government is willing to consider takeovers that would leave Canada's telecom sector with three major companies. That would reverse decades of policy aimed at keeping four competitive national players.

title: OpenAI Asks Judge to Throw Out Tumbler Ridge Shooting Lawsuits and Keep Chat Records Sealed
summary: OpenAI has asked a court to dismiss lawsuits connected to the Tumbler Ridge shooting and to keep the related ChatGPT conversation records sealed. The company argues that conversations with AI deserve the same First Amendment protection as books and video games.

title: Deutsche Telekom Unit Pumps €100M Into Mistral AI
summary: Deutsche Telekom's T.Capital Tech Fund invested €100 million in Mistral AI's recent funding round. The German operator also signalled a future strategic partnership with the French AI company around sovereign infrastructure.

title: Samsung, TSMC Suspend Some China Chip Shipments
summary: TSMC and Samsung Electronics reportedly halted some chip shipments to Chinese companies after the latest U.S. export controls. The move shows the new restrictions spreading through the global semiconductor supply chain.

title: Dell'Oro Sees Q3 Uptick for RAN Revenue
summary: Dell'Oro Group said worldwide radio access network revenue grew at a mid-single-digit rate year over year in the third quarter. It was the market's strongest quarterly performance in nearly five years.

title: GTA 6 Rakes In Over $2.3B at Launch
summary: Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto VI generated more than $2.3 billion from preorders and launch-day sales, after a development budget reported at over $1 billion. Launch livestreams peaked at nearly 7.9 million concurrent viewers. Take-Two is counting on the game to help deliver up to $8.2 billion in fiscal 2027 net bookings.
also_covered_by: The Globe and Mail Business Brief

title: Uber Tests Solo Rides for Tweens
summary: Uber is piloting Uber Kids in Austin, Nashville and Madison, letting parents book unaccompanied rides for children aged 10 to 12. Safeguards include PIN verification at pickup, mandatory audio and video recording, and invite-only drivers who earn $7 more per trip than on UberX. The service competes with HopSkipDrive and follows a failed 2017 Uber pilot.

title: The Brother-Sister Duo Who Want to Keep Anthropic Weird
summary: The WSJ profiles Anthropic co-founders Dario and Daniela Amodei, who saw their company complete the largest IPO on record on Thursday only to face a broad market sell-off the following day. The piece frames the swing as the latest unusual turn for a company that has consistently diverged from conventional corporate norms.

title: The Danger of Jensen Huang’s Handshake Deals at Nvidia
summary: The WSJ examines Jensen Huang's habit of striking informal, no-contract agreements during his time leading Nvidia. Deals he once touted as a strength are now being viewed as red flags following his ouster as CEO amid the company's widening scandal.
